title: The gospel as the rule (1208)
hook: Francis hears Matthew 10 at Mass and decides to live it literally

segments.voice: Yesterday, kissing the leper: Francis showed mercy, and what was bitter became sweet. Your line was bitter became sweet. Did you do the thing you shrink from? Day one thousand two hundred nine.

A small chapel outside Assisi. A Mass. The priest reads the gospel, the same way gospels get read every day, and the room may well have heard this one before. One man in the chapel hasn't heard it like this. It's the passage where Jesus sends his disciples out with almost nothing. When Mass ends, the man goes up to the priest and asks him to explain it. And when the priest is done, he says, in his biographer's telling: this is what I want. This is what I've been looking for. Today: the gospel as the rule.
screen: `A MASS NEAR ASSISI.` → `A FAMILIAR GOSPEL.` → `THIS IS WHAT I WANT.`

segments.voice: Here's the passage, from Matthew, in the Douay-Rheims. Jesus tells the twelve: "Do not possess gold, nor silver, nor money in your purses: Nor scrip for your journey, nor two coats, nor shoes, nor a staff; for the workman is worthy of his meat." A scrip is a traveler's bag. So: no money, no bag, no spare coat, no shoes, no walking stick. Go, and trust that you'll be fed. It is possible to hear words like these as a picture of an attitude: hold things loosely. Francis took them as instructions. According to his early biographer, he took off his shoes on the spot, put down his staff, kept a single tunic, and swapped his leather belt for a piece of rope. Then he started going from place to place, preaching peace and repentance. Later, in his Testament, Francis put it this way: no one showed him what he ought to do, but the Most High himself revealed that he should live according to the form of the holy gospel. That's the turn today is about. Benedict wrote a rule and pointed beyond it to Scripture. Francis tried to skip the middle step. When his brothers later needed a written rule, its opening line said, in effect, that the rule and life of the brothers is this: to observe the holy gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ. The gospel wasn't the inspiration for the rule. It was the rule. The early biographer doesn't say which gospel writer's version was read; the sending passages in Matthew, Mark and Luke are close cousins. What he does tell is the response: he heard it and did it, literally.
screen: `NO GOLD, NO SCRIP, NO TWO COATS.` · `SHOES OFF, STAFF DOWN, A ROPE BELT.` · `THE MOST HIGH REVEALED IT TO ME.` · then, large: `THE GOSPEL WAS THE RULE.` · then: `HE HEARD IT AND DID IT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: take one gospel line literally. Settle, and breathe. Let one gospel line come to mind, one you know well enough that it's gone smooth. Give to the one who asks. Love your enemies. Take nothing for the journey. Hold it the way Francis held his, not as a nice idea, but as an instruction for today. Ask: what would it look like if I did exactly this, once, before the day ends? Let one concrete answer appear. If you pray, you can ask for the nerve to do it. The bell holds the time.
The gospel as the rule. Francis's choice to live the gospel's words as written, starting with the sending of the twelve: take nothing for the journey. Today's word.
screen: `THE GOSPEL AS THE RULE — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: take nothing. Today, leave one thing behind you usually carry, the extra bag, the backup plan, the phone on a short walk, and notice what it's like to go light. Day one thousand two hundred nine.

howItsDone: Franciscan friars take the gospel as their rule of life, and the Rule of Saint Francis opens by naming the observance of the holy gospel as the life of the brothers.

fork.setup: you've just heard Jesus tell his disciples to take no money, no bag, no shoes, no staff. Mass is over. what do you do?
options: admire it, and go home the same.
ask the priest to explain it, then take off your shoes.
write a long commentary on what it might mean.
fork.reveal: in his biographer's telling, Francis asked the priest to explain it, said this is what I want, and did it on the spot.

trapdoor: what you thought: Francis loved the gospel the way anyone might.
what it means: he heard Jesus send the twelve out with nothing, and did exactly that, taking the gospel as his rule.
what a scholar hears: the Franciscan Rule opens by naming the observance of the holy gospel as the life of the brothers.

notes: The title carries the year 1208 from the index; the spoken script states no year by design. Confirm the index date (the event is often dated 1208 or 1209).

Celano, First Life 22, paraphrased: Francis hears the gospel of the sending of the disciples at Mass, asks the priest to explain it, exclaims 'this is what I want…', removes his shoes, puts aside his staff, keeps one tunic, replaces his belt with a cord, and begins preaching. Confirm details and that 'peace and repentance' fits Celano's account. 'A small chapel outside Assisi' (the Portiuncula) is not named; confirm.
'Later, in his Testament' — confirm the Testament postdates the event (it does by tradition).

Testament paraphrase: 'no one showed me what I ought to do, but the Most High himself revealed to me that I should live according to the form of the holy Gospel.' Later Rule ch. 1: 'The Rule and life of the Friars Minor is this: to observe the holy Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ.' Both paraphrased; confirm.
'Accounts differ on which gospel was read' — Celano does not specify Matthew; the index names Matthew 10. Confirm framing.
Practice examples ('give to the one who asks', 'love your enemies') are paraphrases of gospel lines, not quotations.

Editor pass: cut 'weekday' and 'line by line' (not in Celano); 'accounts differ' (an unsupported claim about the sources) replaced with what Celano does and doesn't say, in the teach and the myth item.
